bull.b: The sharp margin expansion indicates a more profitable business mix, supported by digital growth and the restructuring or sale of lower-margin operations. If sustained, stronger unit economics should improve cash generation and help Inspired fund investment and debt reduction.

Meaningfully positive operating and free cash flow gives Inspired an internal source of funding while management actively reduces debt. Continued cash conversion and deleveraging would improve financial flexibility, lower refinancing pressure, and strengthen the company’s ability to invest in growth.

Growth across Interactive, together with reported share gains in important markets, supports the strength of Inspired’s operator distribution and content offering. Broader adoption can create recurring usage-linked revenue and reinforce the company’s position across digital gaming channels.

bear.b: High debt combined with persistent negative equity leaves Inspired with limited financial flexibility relative to its operating scale. The capital structure increases refinancing sensitivity and means a larger share of future cash generation may need to support obligations rather than growth or shareholder returns.

The higher U.K. remote gaming duty directly raises the cost of Interactive revenue and compressed margins despite strong gross gaming revenue growth. Because the tax change is structural, it can weigh on earnings and cash conversion across the medium term unless pricing or operating efficiencies offset it.

Falling trailing revenue and recurring losses reduce confidence that current operating performance will translate into durable bottom-line earnings. Year-to-year volatility also makes planning and debt reduction more dependent on execution, product momentum, and continued margin improvement.
